server.name: Agentic Atlas
server.title: Agentic Atlas: Agent Design Patterns
server.description: Helps an agent design or review an agent system: find the patterns, concepts, examples, decisions, and terms that fit its problem, read their guidance, and follow how they relate, all from one published Agentic Atlas Release through read-only tools.

protocolMetadata.instructions: Consult one active Agentic Atlas Release. Every tool addresses its payload directly: call atlas_cards with the canonical ids you already know, atlas_read for any exact canonical address, and atlas_orient only when you do not yet have an identity. atlas_orient ranks whole-word matches (a word of four or more characters also matches longer words it begins), each word weighed by how few subjects carry it in an identity field: a match in an identity field or a Card claim makes a subject a candidate, a match in Section text makes one only when no subject matches an identity field, and total counts the candidates. A complete Node from atlas_read is prose alone; its relationships come from atlas_links. Carry the coherence marker each payload returns as expected_revision on every later call, so a promotion is refused rather than silently crossed. Use atlas_navigate for the canonical tree or the publisher-curated tour. Every payload's scope.omitted_fact_classes names what it withheld; each class has one fixed recovery: claims via atlas_cards, sections via atlas_read, and links via atlas_links, each addressed at the subject in hand; provenance via atlas_cards with the subject id and provenance=true; decisions via atlas_orient with query='' and kind='decision', then a single decision via atlas_read at the returned 'decision:<decision-id>' address; terms via atlas_orient with kind='term', then optionally atlas_read at the returned 'term:<key>' address. A definition read names that term: subject and declares no omitted fact classes. A truncated collection returns scope.next_cursor; continue it by repeating the same call with cursor.

tool.name: atlas_orient
tool.title: Search Atlas Nodes, Decisions, and Terms
tool.description: Find Atlas entries by topic when you hold no id; an id you already hold can be read directly. Searches Nodes (patterns, concepts, examples) and Roadmap entries (announced, unpublished); kind narrows it to one Node kind, Decisions, or glossary terms. Ids, titles, Hooks (one-line summaries), and claims decide candidacy, Section text only when no subject matches those; order is identity score, then Section score, then how many words matched, then the publisher's order. Returns ranked ids with Hooks (a term's is its whole definition), paged with a cursor. A miss is an empty page; invalid arguments are refused as invalid_argument.

kind.description: Narrows the search to one Node kind, to Decision records, or to glossary terms. Omit it to search every Node kind plus Roadmap entries (announced, unpublished); setting it leaves Roadmap entries out.

bound.description: How many ranked candidates this call returns; raise it to compare more matches at once, and continue past it with cursor.

examples: keep bulky context out of the window

query.description: A topic or question in ordinary design vocabulary. Words match whole words (four or more characters also match longer words they begin; stopwords drop) in canonical ids, titles, Hooks, and claims, then Section headings and bodies; rarer words weigh more. Section text makes a candidate only when no subject matches elsewhere, so total counts the candidates. kind='decision' searches Decision ids, titles, and bodies; kind='term', keys and definitions. Empty lists every subject of the kind.

cursor.description: scope.next_cursor from a prior atlas_orient page; repeat the same other arguments.

status.description: Maturity filter. Published Nodes are 'fleshed' or 'stable'; Roadmap entries may be any rung. Refused with kind 'decision' or 'term'.

expected_revision.description: Pins this call to the Release (published edition) a prior payload named in 'coherence'; refused as 'revision_changed' if the active Release has changed. Omit for the active Release.

data.description: candidates, ranked. A Node candidate has id, status, hook, and disclosure ('full', or 'roadmap' with its title); a Decision or term candidate has id, which is its atlas_read address, and hook.

tool.name: atlas_cards
tool.title: Get Atlas Summary Cards by ID
tool.description: Get one summary Card per Atlas Node id: its Hook (one-line summary) and the publisher's claims (thesis, law, when-to-reach, or claim), each citing its source Sections. Use when you hold ids and want their guidance without full text, such as to compare entries. Cards return in request order. Atomic: one unknown or Roadmap-only (unpublished) id refuses the whole batch as batch_not_atomic, naming the rejected ids.

ids.description: The Nodes to summarize, as bare ids (no '#section') such as atlas_orient candidate ids or atlas_navigate tree ids; Cards return in this order.

provenance.description: true also returns each cited source's content digest and publisher attestation (who, when), plus the Release's digests: a larger response.

expected_revision.description: Pins this call to the Release (published edition) a prior payload named in 'coherence'; refused as 'revision_changed' if the active Release has changed. Omit for the active Release.

data.description: cards, one per requested id in request order: id, title, kind, status, hook, and claims (id, text, field, sources as 'node-id#section-slug'). With provenance=true, also provenance: release (version and digests) and addresses, each with address, dependency_digest, distillation, and attestation (publisher, attested_on).

tool.name: atlas_read
tool.title: Read an Atlas Node, Section, Decision, or Term
tool.description: Read the full text at one exact Atlas address. A bare Node id returns the whole entry: identity, tree position, Hook (one-line summary), and every Section; relationship occurrences are omitted. A Section, Decision, or glossary term address returns that one item. Use when a summary is not enough or you need exact wording to cite. An unknown or malformed address is refused as invalid_argument; a wrong slug's refusal lists the real ones.

address.description: A bare Node id, 'node-id#section-slug', 'decision:<decision-id>', or 'term:<key>'. Slugs are not guessable: read them off a Node's sections, a Card claim's sources, or a Link's occurrence.

expected_revision.description: Pins this call to the Release (published edition) a prior payload named in 'coherence'; refused as 'revision_changed' if the active Release has changed. Omit for the active Release.

data.description: node: identity (id, title, kind, status), hierarchy (parent, ancestors, breadcrumb, sibling_position, sibling_count), hook, and sections (slug, heading, position, content). section: section. decision: decision (id, title, content). definition: term and definition.

tool.name: atlas_links
tool.title: List an Atlas Node's Relationships
tool.description: List where one Atlas Node references other entries (outbound) and where they reference it (inbound), outbound first. Use to find related entries or what points at this one. Each occurrence gives direction, class, source Section, and the far end's Hook (one-line summary), plus its id and title unless the class is 'undisclosed' (unpublished and unannounced). Results are paged: follow the cursor to the end before concluding nothing points here. An unknown or Roadmap-only (unpublished) subject is refused as invalid_argument.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Agentic Atlas: Agent Design Patterns to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Agentic Atlas: Agent Design Patterns to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://agentic-atlas.dev/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Agentic Atlas: Agent Design Patterns MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, Agentic Atlas: Agent Design Patterns scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Agentic Atlas: Agent Design Patterns's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, Agentic Atlas: Agent Design Patterns scores 93/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 5 of 5 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Agentic Atlas: Agent Design Patterns?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Agentic Atlas: Agent Design Patterns in search-research on the Manufact MCP catalog include common-practice, GDELT Cloud, BookDNA, Lyon, and Exa.
